default: BGM is MANDATORY on EVERY blog with NO opt-out and NO `audio.used=false` path (not even for sober / abstract / privacy topics): every story opens with a fitting, REAL, SOURCED background track presented in ONE canonical format — a cover-art card at the TOP of the article, directly BELOW THE TITLE (in-flow, centered, so the reader can't miss it), whose cover is a SPINNING VINYL DISC (the album/track cover rendered as a circular disc that rotates ONLY while playing) + title / artist / description + ONE play/pause button. Every blog ends up with the SAME presentation format (consistency: top-of-article placement + the spinning-vinyl cover). Its job is immersion and mood, not data encoding. The front-of-blog BGM is NEVER AI-composed — it is always a real recording the Scout sourced (sourced_bgm). ALWAYS source a fitting track — including for SOBER topics: a sober / computational / statistical / economic story (economics, elections, public-health stats, finance) gets a restrained pensive / ambient / minimal / orchestral / nocturne track (see mood_word_map), which is the RIGHT BGM there — NOT silence, and NOT 'tonally-wrong filler'. Match the mood word to the story's tone (mood_word_map below); a somber topic gets a quiet, NON-TRIUMPHANT piece with no especially strong emotion. The player autostarts on the reader's FIRST click/tap anywhere on the page (a single first-gesture unlock), then it is reader-controlled via the play/pause button, works fully when muted, and may loop or play once. FIT FIRST is the rule for which track to ship: pick the most recognizable BEST-FIT real track the story carries. If the story has a signature track — an official anthem, a film theme, the song the piece is about — that track IS the best fit, so SOURCE THAT, even when it is copyrighted (rung 2: self-hosted for the DEMO behind a publish-gate — license "All Rights Reserved — demo-only", publish_blocker=true, source_url — never silently shipped as if clean). A license-clean track (CC0 / CC-BY / public-domain / royalty-free, re-hostable and publishable) is preferred only when a clean track fits the story AS WELL as the best-fit track; license-tier is a TIEBREAK among comparably-fitting tracks, never a reason to ship a generic, topically-unrelated CC0 loop in place of the real best-fit anthem. A generic license-clean loop is NOT a win just because it is publishable — a worse-fitting clean track loses to a better-fitting copyrighted one. When NO topic-fitting real track and NO signature track land, the GUARANTEED floor is a LICENSE-CLEAN CLASSICAL RECORDING (rung C below) — so a BGM is ALWAYS present. Work the BGM ladder in `bgm_ladder` (a real sourced track, never AI) on every topic to source the fitting track; the ladder always ends with a track (the classical floor never fails). (text2music is NOT a BGM rung — it is repurposed to opt-in `sound_design` SFX for un-findable sounds; see experience_types.)
placement: TOP OF THE ARTICLE, directly BELOW THE TITLE (in-flow as the opening content block, horizontally CENTERED in the column with margin-inline:auto — never left-pinned). NOT a fixed corner widget: a top-of-article card guarantees the reader notices the BGM (a corner player is easy to miss). It is the ONE canonical BGM presentation on every blog (top-of-article placement + the spinning-vinyl cover). Same placement on every breakpoint.
cover_treatment: spinning vinyl disc — the album / track cover art is rendered as a CIRCULAR disc (border-radius:50%) that ROTATES via a CSS @keyframes spin driven by animation-play-state: it spins ONLY while the audio is playing (animation-play-state:running) and is PAUSED otherwise (animation-play-state:paused); @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) disables the spin entirely (the disc is shown static). The disc replaces the old static square cover; keep a single explicit play/pause button beside it. Never a waveform-bar card.

mood_word_map._doc: Match the BGM mood word to the story's tone before searching (fetch_music.py takes a SINGLE broad word). BGM is sourced on EVERY topic — sober topics get a fitting restrained track, not silence.

bgm_ladder._doc: BGM is MANDATORY on every blog, so this ladder ALWAYS runs AND ALWAYS ENDS WITH A TRACK: it is a ladder of REAL tracks to climb to source the fitting track, not a menu to choose between — and the front BGM is ALWAYS a real sourced recording, never AI-composed. Match the mood word to the story's tone first (see mood_word_map). Climb the rungs in order and stop at the first that succeeds; if rungs 1-3 do not land, the GUARANTEED FLOOR is rung C (a license-clean classical RECORDING), which never fails — so there is NO `audio.used=false` / no-BGM outcome on any topic. The ladder is about HOW to source a track — and a sober topic gets a fitting restrained track (pensive / ambient / minimal / orchestral), not silence.
bgm_ladder.applies_when: EVERY story — BGM is mandatory on every topic, so the ladder always runs and always ends with a track. Match the mood word to the tone (mood_word_map): a SOBER computational / statistical topic (economics, elections, public-health stats, finance) gets a restrained pensive / ambient / minimal / orchestral track, which IS the right fitting BGM there. There is NO `audio.used=false` escape — a privacy-sensitive topic also gets a BGM (a quiet, non-intrusive classical recording fits). Do not skip the ladder, and do not force a celebratory loop onto a sober story — source the fitting restrained track, or fall to the mood-appropriate classical floor (rung C).

rungs.what: A LICENSE-CLEAN real track the Scout found (CC0 / CC-BY / public-domain / royalty-free, re-hostable and PUBLISHABLE) that fits the story's mood AS WELL as any best-fit track, referenced by media_ref -> the Scout sct_xx. Rendered as the now-playing card: square cover art + title / artist / desc + one play/pause button at the very TOP, autostarts on the reader's first click/tap, reader-controlled, works when muted. License + attribution come from scout.json and the attribution renders in the References footer. This rung is preferred ONLY when a clean track genuinely fits the story as well as the best-fit candidate — publishable is a TIEBREAK among comparably-fitting tracks, not a license to swap in a generic, topically-unrelated CC0 loop. FIT FIRST: if the story has a recognizable signature track (an official anthem, a film theme, the song it is about) and the best clean option is a generic loop that fits worse, that real best-fit track wins on rung 2 — do not settle for the clean loop here.
rungs.on_fail: If the Scout found no license-clean re-hostable track that fits AS WELL as the best-fit track (or none fits at all), fall to rung 2 (do NOT stop at audio.used=false here).

rungs.what: A copyrighted best-fit REAL track self-hosted for the DEMO only, behind a publish-gate. Same now-playing-card UX as rung 1. Registered as a Designer `des_` audio asset (NOT claimed as a license-clean `sct_`, so it never lies to the validate.py license gate) carrying license: "All Rights Reserved — demo-only", publish_blocker: true, and the source_url. The Auditor raises an advisory `copyrighted_audio_publish_blocker` (flags but does NOT block the demo build) and the Programmer renders a credits/footer line "demo-only — must license or swap before publishing". This rung is the PREFERRED default whenever the story carries a recognizable best-fit real track (an official anthem, a film theme, the signature song the piece is about) — FIT FIRST: a real best-fit anthem here beats a generic, topically-unrelated CC0 loop on rung 1, because license-tier is only a tiebreak among comparably-fitting tracks. Climb to rung 1 instead only when a license-clean track fits the story AS WELL as this best-fit one (then publishable wins the tie).
rungs.on_fail: If no copyrighted best-fit track can be self-hosted either, fall to rung 3.

rungs.what: Embed the OFFICIAL platform player (Spotify / Apple Music / YouTube oEmbed) for a referenced copyrighted track — the official player carries its own rights, so nothing is re-hosted. Use when the story references a specific real song / anthem / recording you cannot self-host even for a demo. The embed is the played audio here; it does not need the now-playing card.
rungs.on_fail: If no embeddable official player exists for a fitting track either, fall to rung 4.

rungs.what: The GUARANTEED LICENSE-CLEAN FLOOR — reached when no topic-fitting real track (rung 1) and no signature track (rungs 2/3) land. Source a LICENSE-CLEAN CLASSICAL RECORDING. KEY CORRECTNESS POINT: a public-domain *composition* (Beethoven / Bach / Chopin / Tchaikovsky / Mozart / Haydn / Brahms / Debussy / Satie…) is NOT automatically a public-domain *recording* — the score may be PD while a modern performance is fully copyrighted. So the floor must be a license-clean RECORDING of the piece with the RECORDING's own license verified (sourced from PD/CC recording libraries — Musopen, Wikimedia Commons PD/CC audio, IMSLP recordings tab (check each recording's license, not the score's), Free Music Archive CC). Prefer a PERIOD-APPROPRIATE piece (match the topic's era if findable), else a famous master; keep it MOOD-APPROPRIATE (a somber topic gets a quiet, NON-TRIUMPHANT piece with no especially strong emotion — a nocturne / adagio / Gymnopédies / slow movement; never a triumphant fanfare). Rendered in the SAME top-of-article spinning-vinyl card. Registered as a clean `sct_` audio item (the verified recording license is on the allowlist, so it passes the validate.py license gate). This rung ALWAYS succeeds, so every blog ends with a license-clean BGM. The classical floor is REAL recordings — NEVER AI-composed.
rungs.on_fail: Does not fail — a license-clean classical recording is always findable. (If the only available recording of a chosen piece is itself copyrighted, that is a copyrighted track: demo-gate it on rung 2 / embed on rung 3, and keep choosing pieces until a license-clean RECORDING lands.)

bgm_ladder.never_ai_composed: The front-of-blog BGM is NEVER AI-composed / text2music-generated. There is no 'generated' rung. text2music is repurposed to opt-in `sound_design` SFX (see experience_types) and must never be used as the front BGM.
bgm_ladder.copyrighted_referenced_track: A copyrighted REFERENCED track that the STORY IS ABOUT (an official anthem, a viral hit) IS the best-fit mood track by definition, so FIT FIRST prefers self-hosting it on rung 2 (a des_ asset with publish_blocker:true, demo-gated) so the reader can actually HEAR the track the piece is about — a generic license-clean loop does not substitute for it. Fall back to rung 3 (embed the official platform player) only when even a demo self-host is impossible. It is never silently re-hosted as a license-clean sct_ item, and it is never dropped in favour of a topically-unrelated CC0 loop just to stay publishable.

purpose_first: Audio must serve ONE of two purposes, stated explicitly in the brief: IMMERSE (a real sourced background track that sets mood and aids reading — MANDATORY on every blog, including a restrained track on a sober topic and a quiet classical recording on a privacy topic; opt-in `sound_design` SFX may layer atmosphere) or INFORM (a real embedded recording, or — rarely — a sonification that genuinely lets the ear decode a pattern). The front BGM always serves IMMERSE and is always present; any ADDITIONAL audio idea that serves neither, drop it — never add sound just to tick the audio channel.
questions_before_choosing: What is the story's TONE — triumphant, somber, tense, or sober/computational? Match the BGM mood word to it (mood_word_map): epic / anthem for triumphant, elegy / adagio for somber, pensive / ambient / minimal / orchestral for a sober numbers story (an inflation series, an election swing, a mortality-rate trend). Then source a real track that fits and present it in the top-of-article spinning-vinyl card (below the title) -> sourced_bgm. BGM is MANDATORY on every topic; a sober story gets a fitting restrained track, a privacy topic a quiet classical recording — never silence.

Does the blog reference real songs, artists, performances, anthems, speeches, or recordings? -> embed the real thing (or, for a best-fit copyrighted mood track, self-host for the demo behind a publish-gate)

Is there a genuinely interpretable sonic pattern a reader could DECODE by ear (not just 'tones falling down a ranking'), tightly synced to a visual that highlights each value as it sounds? -> sonification (rare)

Is there a specific sound the story needs that has NO findable real recording (e.g. an atmospheric tension drone, a glass-shatter texture)? -> opt-in sound_design SFX via text2music (event/section-bound, never the front BGM)
Are there small interaction moments (reveal, completion) where a subtle cue adds tactility? -> ambient cue

experience_types.sourced_bgm: MANDATORY on every blog. A real, sourced background track played as the front-of-blog BGM in the ONE canonical format: a cover-art card at the TOP of the article, directly BELOW THE TITLE (in-flow, centered with margin-inline:auto — never left-pinned, never a fixed corner widget), whose cover is a SPINNING VINYL DISC (circular disc that rotates ONLY while playing — animation-play-state, paused when not playing, spin disabled under prefers-reduced-motion) + title / artist / description + ONE play/pause button. The reader's FIRST click/tap anywhere autostarts it; after that it is reader-controlled via the button, works fully when muted, and may loop or play once. NEVER AI-composed. Prefer a license-clean re-hostable track (publishable); a copyrighted best-fit track may be self-hosted for the demo behind a publish-gate (license "All Rights Reserved — demo-only", publish_blocker:true, source_url); when neither lands, the GUARANTEED FLOOR is a license-clean classical RECORDING (rung C, verify the recording's license). Reference a license-clean track via media_ref (sct_xx) — its license + attribution come from scout.json and render in the References footer; register a copyrighted demo track as a Designer `des_` asset with the publish_blocker. Place the card at the very TOP of the article (set this item's section to the opening / masthead) and horizontally center it. If the Scout could not fetch a license-clean square cover, use a designed CSS disc fallback (NOT AI-generated).
experience_types.embed: Spotify / Apple Music / YouTube embed — when the blog references real songs, artists, albums, playlists, podcasts, speeches, anthems, or recorded performances (including the official theme/anthem or a viral hit you must not re-host). The official player carries its own rights. Provide the URI or embed URL.
experience_types.sonification: RARE. Data sonification only when the data has a genuinely interpretable sonic structure the ear can decode AND it is tightly bound to a visual that highlights each value as it sounds. 'Play the ranking as falling tones' is NOT interpretable — do not do it; use a real sourced background track instead. When you do sonify, specify the mapping, legend, tempo, and the synced visual.
experience_types.sound_design: OPT-IN. An atmospheric sound-design bed / SFX (text2music, e.g. google/lyria-3-pro-preview) for a sound the story needs that has NO findable real recording — drones, textures, ambience, room tone; sharp foley (e.g. bullet-on-glass) is best-effort (the model's strength is ambient beds, not crisp transients). It is event-bound or section-bound, short, reader-controlled, has a visual/mute equivalent, and is NEVER the front-of-blog BGM (the BGM is always a real sourced track). Register it as a Designer `des_` audio asset. Use sparingly and only when a real recording genuinely cannot be sourced.
experience_types.ambient: Ambient audio cue — short sound effects tied to interactions (hover, scroll reveal, drag, completion). Use sparingly, mute toggle, always a visual equivalent.
experience_types.none: RETIRED for the front BGM — there is NO 'no-BGM' outcome. BGM is MANDATORY on EVERY blog (including sober / abstract / privacy topics): the ladder always lands a track, and its rung-C classical-recording floor never fails, so audio.used is always true. A privacy-sensitive topic gets a quiet, non-intrusive classical recording, NOT silence. (A sober computational/statistical/economic/elections/health-stats story gets a fitting restrained track — pensive / ambient / minimal / orchestral.) `none` is no longer a valid front-BGM state.

audio_form_rules._note: audio_type should determine both the experience and the layout. The front BGM is ALWAYS a real SOURCED background track presented in the top-of-article spinning-vinyl card, directly below the title (mandatory, one canonical format on every blog); reach for sonification only in the rare genuinely-interpretable case, and for sound_design SFX only when a needed sound has no findable real recording.
audio_form_rules.sourced_bgm: The cover-art card at the TOP of the article, directly BELOW THE TITLE (in-flow as the opening content block, centered with margin-inline:auto — never left-pinned, never a fixed corner widget), whose cover is a SPINNING VINYL DISC — a circular disc that spins ONLY while playing (animation-play-state; paused otherwise; spin disabled under prefers-reduced-motion) + title / artist / desc + one play/pause button. A top-of-article card guarantees the reader notices the BGM. Autostarts on the reader's first click/tap, then reader-controlled, works when muted, may loop or play once. NEVER AI-composed. For a license-clean track pull the file + its license/attribution from the Scout's sct_xx (media_ref) and render the attribution as a credit line in the References footer; for a copyrighted demo track register a `des_` asset with publish_blocker:true and render the demo-only footer note. Disc art comes from a license-clean square image the Scout fetched, else a designed CSS disc fallback (not AI). Avoid the generic 'audio card + waveform bars'.
audio_form_rules.embed: Native platform embed or a compact listening inset. Best for real tracks, performances, podcasts, speeches, anthems, recorded examples — the official player carries its own rights, so it is the way to feature a referenced copyrighted song without re-hosting.
audio_form_rules.sonification: Only if genuinely interpretable. Make the sound data-bound and explanatory, paired with a chart/timeline/stepper that visibly highlights the value being heard. Specify scale, legend, tempo, how readers compare values. Never generic tones with no decodable mapping.
audio_form_rules.sound_design: An opt-in atmospheric SFX bed for an un-findable sound, event-triggered or section-bound, short, with a mute toggle and a visual equivalent. Distinct from the front BGM — it is a small section-bound element, not the top-of-article spinning-vinyl BGM card. Register as a `des_` audio asset. Never used as the front-of-blog BGM.
audio_form_rules.ambient: A small optional cue tied to an interaction, mute toggle, no central card. The page must work fully without sound.
audio_form_rules.none: RETIRED — no longer a valid front-BGM state. BGM is mandatory on every blog and the ladder always lands a real track (the rung-C classical-recording floor never fails). There is no audio.used=false outcome on any topic, privacy included.

web_weight: The BGM the reader streams must be web-weight: audio < 3 MB (shared budget with the Auditor weight-gate; image < 600 KB, video < 3 MB). A big WAV/FLAC — e.g. the Scout's sourced_bgm `scout_*` track — MUST be transcoded to ~128 kbps mp3/opus BEFORE you reference it: run `python3 SKILL_DIR/scripts/optimize_assets.py PROJECT_DIR/assets/` (uses ffmpeg if available; warns and skips without crashing if not), then point the audio item's `filename` at the optimized `_web` copy while keeping `media_ref` → the Scout `sct_xx` (its license/identity stay in scout.json). The same transcode applies to a self-hosted copyrighted demo track. Never reference a multi-MB lossless BGM directly — it is a performance and virality killer. If the helper had to skip transcoding (no codec), note the original is over budget so the Auditor catches it rather than shipping it.
novelty: Vary the sourced TRACK's character across blogs (don't ship the same soundtrack vibe), but the PLAYER FORM is FIXED and CONSISTENT — every blog uses the same top-of-article spinning-vinyl card (below the title) (that consistency is intentional, not sameness to avoid). Don't fall back to a click-to-play tone card.
what_to_specify: Type: sourced_bgm (real sourced track in the top-of-article spinning-vinyl card below the title, MANDATORY on every blog — license-clean preferred, copyrighted-demo behind a publish-gate, license-clean classical recording as the guaranteed floor) / embed (official player for a copyrighted referenced track) / sonification (rare) / sound_design (opt-in SFX for an un-findable sound, never the BGM) / ambient. (`none` is retired — BGM is mandatory, the ladder always lands a track.)
Purpose: IMMERSE (the mood it sets and why it aids THIS story) or INFORM (what the ear actually learns)
Trigger: BGM autostarts on the reader's FIRST click/tap, then play/pause; never autoplay before a gesture. Loop or play-once a background track. SFX is event/section-bound.

Content: filename + media_ref (sct_xx) + cover image for a license-clean sourced_bgm; filename + license "All Rights Reserved — demo-only" + publish_blocker:true + source_url + cover for a copyrighted demo track; Spotify URI for embed; data mapping + synced visual for sonification; prompt + tool + model for sound_design SFX; cue description for ambient
Web weight: the referenced audio file is < 3 MB — transcode a big WAV/FLAC to ~128 kbps mp3/opus via optimize_assets.py and reference the optimized _web copy (keep media_ref → sct_xx)
Fallback: the page must work fully when muted or unsupported; the disc cover falls back to a designed CSS disc (not AI)
Novelty note: how this audio TRACK differs from recent blogs (the player FORM is fixed/consistent — the top-of-article spinning-vinyl card on every blog)
UI form: the top-of-article spinning-vinyl BGM card below the title (always, for the front BGM), platform embed, chart-synced sonification, opt-in SFX element, or subtle interaction cue
